question: Knowing what is known at the review date, would we write materially different protections for this borrower?

evidence_attributable_changes.rationale: Evidence shows $8M write-off of excess component inventory in Q4 2024, indicating inventory management challenges that could overstate core assets and increase cash consumption.
evidence_attributable_changes.change: Increase the Minimum Core Assets Test threshold to provide a buffer against potential inventory overstatement.

evidence.quote: Additionally, we recorded an incremental non-recurring charge in the fourth quarter of $8 million related to the write-off of excess component inventory and losses on non-cancelable purchase commitments

updated_summary: At the review date, only the Minimum Core Assets Test (C01) requires tightening to buffer against inventory overstatement risk shown by an $8M write-off of excess component inventory in Q4 2024. All other clauses (C02‑C05) are retained as no new evidence justifies change. This constitutes a material drift.
updated_reasons: The tightened threshold for C01 addresses inventory overstatement risk evidenced by a Q4 2024 $8M write-off, altering risk coverage and thus constituting material drift.
reading: Changes listed as evidence-attributable appear only when the new reports are supplied. Changes also present in the control reflect pre-existing gaps or model drafting preference, not newly emerging drift. One run of each; repeat-run stability is not yet measured.
